prompt: A clean physics-exam BALLISTIC diagram: a ball is launched from ground level over flat ground, with a horizontal ground ruler marked in metres beneath the trajectory. The launch speed is v0 = 25 metres per second, the launch angle is 27 degrees above the horizontal, and gravity g = 9.8 metres per second squared. Draw the parabolic flight path and mark where the ball LANDS on the ground ruler. Using the range formula R equals v0 squared times sine of (2 times the angle) divided by g, compute the horizontal range and place the landing mark at that computed distance on the metre scale, with the range value labelled. Note the angle is 27 degrees, NOT 45 degrees, so this is not the maximum possible range. Neat black-on-white exam figure; the launch speed, the 27-degree angle and the computed landing range all labelled, the metre ticks legible, no worked steps or extra text.
